components.css: .ds-course-card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; min-width: 18em; max-width: 20em; background: var(--card-color, rgb(180, 227, 240)); border-radius: 12px; box-shadow: 0px 0px 10px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.2); color: var(--text-color, rgb(15, 65, 105)); font-family: Inter, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; overflow: hidden; transition: transform 0.25s ease, box-shadow 0.25s ease; } .ds-course-card-photo { width: 100%; height: 8em; background: linear-gradient(145deg, rgb(108, 161, 205), rgb(15, 65, 105)); border-radius: 10px 10px 0 0; box-shadow: 0px 4px 4px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.25); } .ds-course-card-title { font-size: 24px; font-weight: 600; margin: 8px 12px; text-align: center; } .ds-course-card-links { display: flex; justify-content: space-evenly; gap: 6px; width: 100%; padding: 0 8px 12px; } .ds-course-card .ds-btn-link { padding: 8px; border-radius: 6px; color: var(--background-color, rgb(108, 161, 205)); background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid var(--background-color, rgb(108, 161, 205)); cursor: pointer; transition: all 0.25s ease; } .ds-course-card .ds-btn-link:hover { background: var(--background-color, rgb(108, 161, 205)); color: #ffffff; } .ds-course-card:hover { transform: scale(1.05); box-shadow: 0px 8px 16px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.25); } .ds-course-card:hover .ds-course-card-photo { filter: grayscale(80%); }

narrative.overview:
This is a personal teaching catalog seen in daylight. Marc is the face; the sky is atmosphere, not a mountaineering story. Pages feel generous and handmade: large Inter, lots of air, photography in the first viewport, centered columns that breathe rather than pack. The blue field is a classroom window — calm, open, a little weathered — not a brand illustration of peaks and rope.

Density is low on purpose. A visitor should feel they can pick a course the way they pick a book off a sunlit table: tiles sit up off the wash, scale when hovered, and send them out to Udemy or Tuto. The wordmark is a Knewave lockup in white on Classroom Sky; everything else is Inter. Do not drift toward SaaS dashboards, dense admin grids, or corporate navy/orange kits.
keyCharacteristics: Photography leads; Classroom Sky is atmosphere behind it, not a motif to decorate.
Inter ExtraBold is the type system; Knewave exists only as the Altitude wordmark.
Generous padding, centered measure, justified body — personal, not editorial-magazine.
Catalog cards lift with real shadows and scale on hover; they must feel pickable.
Two chromatic roles only: Ink Navy for voice and action, Classroom Sky for fields.

rules.name: The Two Blues Rule
rules.body: Ink Navy speaks and acts. Classroom Sky is the room. Do not introduce a third chromatic accent (orange, teal, gold, “CTA red”).

rules.name: The Atmosphere Not Alpine Rule
rules.body: These blues are daylight in a classroom, not glacier branding. Mountain photographs may appear as photography; they do not authorize ice palettes, rope motifs, or sherpa illustration.

rules.name: The Knewave Lockup Rule
rules.body: Knewave appears only on the Altitude wordmark in the header. Do not set headings, buttons, or body in Knewave.

rules.name: The Inter Is the System Rule
rules.body: The root stack currently declares Poppin, which is not loaded, so Helvetica renders. That is a miss, not a face. New type uses Inter.

rules.name: The Lifted Catalog Rule
rules.body: Surfaces that can be chosen (parcours, course, CTA-adjacent tiles) use the shadow vocabulary above. Do not add neumorphic inner highlights. Do not go fully flat.

dos: Do lead a surface with photography and a short Inter ExtraBold line, then the catalog.
Do keep pickable tiles on Lesson Card with the lifted-catalog shadows and a scale hover.
Do use Ink Navy for text and the filled CTA, Classroom Sky for header/footer/wash.
Do reserve Knewave for the Altitude wordmark.
Do leave air: 12/24px rhythm, large section insets, ~80% measure.
donts: Don't design SaaS dashboards, dense data grids, or navy/orange corporate kits.
Don't add a third accent color or reuse the home three-column neumorphic glow.
Don't set headings or UI in Knewave, or treat Poppin/Helvetica as a body face.
Don't turn mountain photographs into sherpa illustration, clipart, or alpine ornament.
Don't invent input, chip, or modal chrome — the catalog does not have forms.
